name: AI surface product lead
oneLine: Runs a chat or search surface (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot); wants conversion, trust and clear liability.
goals: Let users complete a purchase inside the conversation with a checkout that finishes in one or two turns.
Onboard many merchants through one protocol (ACP or UCP) instead of bespoke integrations.
Stay out of the merchant-of-record role: the merchant keeps orders, taxes, returns and compliance.
Prove to users and regulators that the agent bought what the user asked for and nothing else.
Carry a payment credential through checkout without ever holding raw card data.
Measure attribution: which recommendations led to orders, and what the platform earns from them.
pains: Instant Checkout in its 2025 form was scaled back because merchants wanted their own checkout, so the surface now sends traffic out and loses control of the final step.
Liability for a wrong or disputed agent purchase is not settled by Visa or Mastercard rules, and the platform is the most visible party to blame.
Each merchant supports a different subset of capabilities and payment handlers, so the checkout experience varies and negotiation adds latency.
Prompt injection on merchant pages and in product feeds can bias the agent, and users will hold the platform responsible.
Merchants object that platform checkout bypasses their pixels and customer data, and some have gone to court over scraping (Amazon v. Perplexity).
Governance of ACP and UCP sits with a few firms, one of which may be a direct competitor.
decisions: Which commerce protocol to adopt as primary, and whether to support both ACP and UCP.
Whether to host checkout inside the surface or hand off to the merchant with a continue_url.
Which credential providers and PSPs can supply payment tokens to the surface.
What user-intent proof (an AP2 mandate, Verifiable Intent, or nothing beyond a scoped token) to require before a payment.
How to rank and disclose sponsored or affiliate results inside agent recommendations.
